member_of.name: Ike & Tina Turner (Bonnie O'Farrell, first white singer)

podcast.title: Formation and Marriage (1967)
podcast.body: Delaney Bramlett, a guitar player for the `Shindig` TV show house band, met Bonnie O'Farrell at a bowling alley in Los Angeles in 1967. Bonnie, from East St. Louis, Illinois, dropped out of school at 14 to pursue a music career and was the first white singer for Ike & Tina Turner. They had instant chemistry and married seven days after meeting. "Delinean Bramlett was a guitar player for the house band for the TV show Shindig when he met Bonnie O'Farrell at a bowling alley in Los Angeles in 1967."

podcast.title: Stax Records Signing (1968)
podcast.body: In 1968, Delaney & Bonnie signed with the legendary Stax Records in Memphis, an experience that infused their music with a strong soul influence even after they left the label. "In 1968 Delinean Bonnie signed with the legendary stacks records and Memphis and you can hear that soul influence in their music even after they left stacks."

podcast.title: Absence from Festival Express Footage
podcast.body: Despite their importance, there is no known film footage of Delaney & Bonnie performing or interacting on the Festival Express. "I am not sure how that how drunk the cameraman had to be to not get film footage of Delinean and Bonnie."

podcast.title: Bonnie Bramlett on `Roseanne`
podcast.body: Bonnie Bramlett played a character named Bonnie, Roseanne Barr's co-worker, on the 1980s sitcom `Roseanne`. "She played Rosanne's co-worker, Bonnie."

podcast.title: Influence on American Roots Rock
podcast.body: Their collaborative approach to music, borrowing songs and band members, and their eclectic style blending Southern rock, gospel, and soul, were instrumental in pushing rock music back toward American roots traditions. This direction became central to 1970s music through artists like The Allman Brothers, The Band, and Lynyrd Skynyrd. "This song and the entire on tour album is going to help push rock back toward American roots traditions."

podcast.title: Loose Band Lineup
podcast.body: Delaney & Bonnie were known for their flexible band lineup, often functioning as a jam band with live jam sessions, where members could include anyone who was around. "And to say band is kind of a loose term because in addition to Delinean and Bonnie Bramlett, the band could have been anyone who was around."

podcast.title: Members Joined Derek and the Dominos
podcast.body: Following the dissolution of Cream, Eric Clapton formed Derek and the Dominos, incorporating members from Delaney and Bonnie. "he formed Derek and the Dominoes using members of Delaney and Bonnie and Blind Faith."
